CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ready to quit smoking.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old patient presents motivated to quit smoking. Patient has been smoking since high school, initially experimentally with friends and at parties, progressing to daily use. Currently smoking 1.5 packs per day with first cigarette within 1 hour of waking. Patient previously attempted to quit by going cold turkey and was successful for almost a year but relapsed due to work-related stress from layoffs and increased work responsibilities. Patient is now motivated to quit due to impending fatherhood, with daughter expected any day. Patient is concerned about stress as a trigger and has recently started meditation and joined a gym to help manage stress and support smoking cessation efforts. Patient interested in using nicotine patch based on friends' successful experience.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No acute symptoms reported. Patient denies using other tobacco products.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes
Gout
Systolic murmur (previously noted, being monitored)

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol (for gout management)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Smoking: 1.5 packs per day for approximately 26 years. Recent lifestyle changes include starting meditation practice and joining gym. Recently married with baby daughter expected imminently. Works in environment with recent organizational stress. Birthday is next Monday, planned as quit date.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: BP 128/88, HR 68, RR 16, SpO2 98% on room air
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, 2/6 systolic murmur noted (previously known, monitoring continues)
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally, no expiratory wheezes, no rales or rhonchi
Neck: No lymphadenopathy, no carotid bruits appreciated

RESULTS
None documented at this visit.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine dependence: Start 21 mg nicotine patch on Monday (quit date). Change patch location daily to avoid skin irritation. Plan to taper dose over time. Follow-up in 2 weeks to reassess dosage. Continue meditation and exercise as stress management strategies. Monitor stress related to work and impending fatherhood. Patient given handouts on common smoking triggers.
2. Type 2 diabetes: Continue management with diet and exercise. Order hemoglobin A1c for next visit in 2 weeks.
3. Gout: Continue allopurinol. Continue dietary modifications to manage uric acid levels.
4. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks.
